title: Regularity descends along faithfully flat ring maps
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings which is faithfully flat [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map], and assume $S$ is a regular ring [def-weil-regular-scheme] (Noetherian, with every localization at a prime ideal a regular local ring). Then $R$ is a regular ring; in particular $R$ is Noetherian.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 07NG (lemma-descent-regular, line 46715) and its proof (Lemma Tag 033E lemma-descent-Noetherian; Lemma Tag 00OF lemma-flat-under-regular for R_p -> S_q)

proof.text: ($R$ is Noetherian.) A regular ring is Noetherian by definition [def-weil-regular-scheme], so $S$ is Noetherian. Since $\varphi$ is faithfully flat, $R$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-descent-noetherian] (Stacks Lemma 033E: an ascending chain $I_0\subseteq I_1\subseteq\dots$ of ideals of $R$ gives a chain $I_nS$ that stabilizes, and $I=\varphi^{-1}(IS)$ for every ideal $I$ of $R$).

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07NG (lemma-descent-regular, line 46715), first sentence; Lemma Tag 033E (lemma-descent-Noetherian, line 46647)

proof.text: (A prime of $S$ over a given prime of $R$.) Let $\mathfrak p\subset R$ be a prime ideal. Since $\varphi$ is faithfully flat, the map $\operatorname{Spec}S\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is surjective [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-surjective-spectrum], so there is a prime ideal $\mathfrak q\subset S$ with $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)=\mathfrak p$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07NG (lemma-descent-regular, line 46715), second sentence ('Choose a prime q of S lying over p'); Lemma Tag 00HQ (lemma-ff-rings, line 9164)

proof.text: ($R_{\mathfrak p}\to S_{\mathfrak q}$ is a flat local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings.) A faithfully flat ring map is flat [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map]. Hence, by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-ring-maps] applied to the flat map $\varphi$, the prime $\mathfrak q$ and $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$, the induced map of localizations [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] $\varphi_{\mathfrak q}:R_{\mathfrak p}\to S_{\mathfrak q}$, $r/s\mapsto\varphi(r)/\varphi(s)$, is a flat local homomorphism of local rings; as $R$ (Step 1) and $S$ are Noetherian, $R_{\mathfrak p}$ and $S_{\mathfrak q}$ are Noetherian local rings (same node).

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07NG (lemma-descent-regular, line 46715), third sentence ('Lemma 00OF applies to R_p -> S_q'): the hypotheses of 00OF; Lemma Tag 00HT (lemma-flat-localization, line 9196)

proof.text: ($R_{\mathfrak p}$ is regular.) Since $S$ is a regular ring, its localization $S_{\mathfrak q}$ at the prime $\mathfrak q$ is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme]. By Step 3, $\varphi_{\mathfrak q}:R_{\mathfrak p}\to S_{\mathfrak q}$ is a flat local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings with regular target, so $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is a regular local ring by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-under-regular].

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07NG (lemma-descent-regular, line 46715), third sentence; Lemma Tag 00OF (lemma-flat-under-regular, line 27188)

proof.text: (Conclusion.) $R$ is Noetherian (Step 1) and, $\mathfrak p$ being an arbitrary prime of $R$, every localization $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is a regular local ring (Step 4); this is the definition of a regular ring [def-weil-regular-scheme].

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07NG (lemma-descent-regular, line 46715), last sentence; Definition Tag 00OD (definition-regular)
